why: Moves the flag's assignment back below `setState`'s early return, where it sat until this change. `playing` and `launch` both return before it, so the outcome -> playing transition -- the ordinary restart -- left the flag stuck `true` and every later push re-rendered the outcome lines and rewrote the action button behind an already-hidden panel. The natural placement, since every other line of that function's body is below the return; only a test that pushes an outcome DURING play can see it, because `.hud-panel` hides the result either way.
killedBy: hud: versus results (n-player arc PR 4 -- FFA + teams, .hud-coop-kills precedent) a push during PLAY repaints nothing -- the surface gate survives a restart
